title: bash
description: Input schema for the litany built-in `bash` tool (ARCH §3.3, §12 v0.3 toolset). The harness sends this verbatim as the `input_schema` field of the tool's entry in the model call's `tools: [...]` array.

command.description: The whole shell command to run, as one string. It is passed verbatim to `sh -c` on this machine, so pipes, redirection, globbing, `&&` and quoting all work and escaping is yours to get right. It runs non-interactively — stdin is /dev/null, there is no TTY, and it runs to completion; there is no prompt to answer and no way to send it input afterwards. It starts in your current working directory — your worktree unless you moved it with the `cd` tool — and its shell state (cwd, exported variables, functions) is discarded when it exits, so chain what must share state into this one string, or use the `cd` tool to move for more than one call. The result you get back states the exit code on its first line (`Exit code: N`), then stdout, then — whenever the command wrote any, whether it succeeded or failed — its stderr under a `--- stderr ---` marker (ARCH §3.3 result envelope).
